subject.title: [Bug]: The project won't start on Windows and WSL.

question: Should OpenClaw pursue a broad tsdown-to-tsc rollback for this Windows/WSL build hang, or require live current-main repro proof before choosing a narrower dependency, pin, timeout, or wrapper fix?
rationale: The screenshot is credible, but the report lacks full current-main Windows/WSL logs and asks for a build-system direction that affects release and source-build behavior beyond one local patch.

options.title: Require focused Windows/WSL repro first
options.body: Run or request first-build and second-build logs on current main for native Windows and WSL before choosing between dependency update, pin, timeout, cleanup fix, or rollback.

options.title: Treat as beta-blocking build work
options.body: Promote the issue immediately as build-owner work and let maintainers choose the rollback or wrapper direction before full repro isolation.

options.title: Defer until reporter logs are complete
options.body: Keep the issue open but wait for full logs and environment details because the current evidence does not isolate the dependency or local state.

recommendation.title: Require focused Windows/WSL repro first
recommendation.body: Run or request first-build and second-build logs on current main for native Windows and WSL before choosing between dependency update, pin, timeout, cleanup fix, or rollback.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent history makes `vincentkoc` the strongest current owner for Windows tsdown wrapper process handling and related script behavior.
